summary: Make MemoryStorage atomic like JSONStorage: any exception during update/remove/insert_multiple (and Table equivalents) rolls back in-memory changes and invalidates the query cache.

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB instance with MemoryStorage containing [{'name': 'a', 'tmp': 1}, {'name': 'b'}]
acceptance_criteria.when: db.update(delete('tmp')) is called and raises KeyError

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB instance with MemoryStorage containing [{'name': 'a', 'tmp': 1}, {'name': 'b'}]
acceptance_criteria.when: db.remove(Query().tmp.exists()) is called and the user-supplied condition raises an exception (e.g. a custom test function that raises)
acceptance_criteria.then: db.all() returns the original two documents unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB instance with MemoryStorage containing [{'name': 'a'}]
acceptance_criteria.when: db.insert_multiple([{'name': 'b'}, {'invalid': 'doc'}]) is called and the second document causes an exception during insertion (e.g. a storage-level validation error)

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB instance with MemoryStorage where db.search(Query().tmp.exists()) returned [{'name': 'a', 'tmp': 1}] and the cache is populated
acceptance_criteria.when: db.update(delete('tmp')) is called and raises KeyError
acceptance_criteria.then: a subsequent db.search(Query().tmp.exists()) returns [] (cache invalidated, matches rolled-back data)

acceptance_criteria.given: the same test sequence as AC-1 run against a TinyDB instance with JSONStorage (file-backed)
acceptance_criteria.then: the JSON file on disk is unchanged and db.all() returns the original data

assumptions.assumption: "remove / insert_multiple" in the issue refers to TinyDB.remove(), TinyDB.insert_multiple() and their Table equivalents.
Any exception raised during a write operation triggers rollback and cache invalidation.
